title: Stationarity of the loop state
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be a finite binary string, and let $C$ be a configuration of its halting recognizer on $x$ whose state is the loop state. For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, running the recognizer for $t$ steps from $C$ returns $C$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$C$ is a configuration of the halting recognizer on $x$
The state of $C$ is the loop state
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite-state binary-alphabet Turing machine and $M^{\mathrm{acc}}$
its halting recognizer, a machine with a distinguished loop state $\ell$ in
which it moves no head, writes and emits nothing, and remains in $\ell$. For
every input $x$, every configuration $C$ of $M^{\mathrm{acc}}$ on $x$ whose state
is $\ell$, and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, running $M^{\mathrm{acc}}$ for $t$ steps
from $C$ yields $C$ itself; in particular it never halts.
